citations.quote: KRAS G12C, TP53 R273C, STK11 loss, PD‑L1 TPS 10 %

candidates.description: The percentage of tumor cells showing membrane staining for PD-L1, used to guide immunotherapy and targeted therapy decisions.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numerical percentage associated with 'PD-L1 TPS' or 'PD-L1 expression'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Percentage (%) of tumor cells expressing PD-L1.
candidates.name: PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: The specific IHC assay used for measurement is not consistently specified across all entries.

candidates.description: The increase in the number of copies of the MET gene in tumor cells, which may render the tumor susceptible to MET inhibitors.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numerical value associated with 'MET Amplification' (copy number) or 'MET copy-number gain' (fold-increase).
candidates.measurement_definition: Measured as either the absolute copy number or the fold-increase relative to diploid.
candidates.name: MET Gene Amplification
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence provides both absolute copy number and fold-increase, which may require standardization for combined analysis.

limitations: Small sample of patient records provided.
Inconsistent reporting units for MET amplification (copy number vs. fold-increase).
summary: The evidence identifies several baseline molecular and clinical variables in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), including PD-L1 expression levels, MET gene amplification status, and ECOG performance status.
